system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager

# OUTPUT 1: CV
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Site Reliability / Platform Engineer
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior SRE and platform engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years running
Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in hands-on cloud infrastructure engineering, Terraform, platform
design and operation, and leading technical work across product and platform teams. Builds reliable, observable
platforms and self-service infrastructure that help teams deploy and operate services effectively.
CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), cloud environment
design and operation
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane
Platforms and deployment: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error
budgets, incident management
Programming and systems: Go, Python, Bash, Linux, Puppet
Testing: k6
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS) | Manchester / remote Apr 2022 –
Present
• Tech lead for a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters and three
regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
• Designed and built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and
Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3. Adopted by all 14 product teams; reduced the time for a new
service to reach production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
• Led the move from cluster-autoscaler managed node groups to Karpenter, using Spot instances for stateless
workloads with interruption handling. Reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately £410,000 per year).
• Introduced SLOs and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services, with error-budget policy agreed with
product leadership. Reduced on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
• Serve in the incident commander rotation and established incident and post-mortem processes.
Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games | Leeds Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
• Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure (EC2, ECS and later EKS) for titles with up to 1.2 million daily
active players.
• Managed infrastructure as code in Terraform across approximately 40 modules, using Atlantis for plan and
apply through pull requests.
• Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
• Ran k6 load tests and launch-day capacity planning, including tests simulating 300,000 concurrent players;
identified and helped resolve a connection-pool limit before launch.
Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting | Sheffield Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
• Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
• Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.
SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes preview namespace cleanup operator | Open source side project 2024
• Built a small Go Kubernetes controller using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; received
approximately 120 GitHub stars.
EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016
CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023
ADDITIONAL
Speaker, UK DevOps meetup (2024): “SLOs that product managers care about”
Mentored three engineers transitioning from backend engineering into SRE
Languages: English (native), Urdu (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility hiring team,
I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role. I bring 10 years of
infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and a
track record of turning infrastructure needs into reliable platforms that product teams can use
effectively.
At Tallybrook, I’m the technical lead of a five-person platform team operating eight EKS
clusters across three regions. At Brightwater Games, I managed Terraform across approximately
40 AWS modules, using Atlantis to run plan and apply through pull requests. I designed and
built an internal developer platform adopted by all 14 product teams, reducing the time for a
new service to reach production from around two weeks to under one day. I’ve also led technical
work across teams, including a Karpenter migration that reduced EC2 spend by 38%, and
introduced SLOs and an incident process that helped reduce on-call pages by approximately
60%. As technical lead, I have led platform decisions across product and platform teams,
including agreeing an error-budget policy with product leadership and introducing service
templates and self-service infrastructure that all 14 product teams adopted.
Corvale’s work to connect a new train fleet with cloud services calls for careful infrastructure
design, operational reliability and collaboration across engineering teams. My background in
hands-on AWS infrastructure engineering and cloud environment design and operation,
Terraform, Kubernetes platforms, observability and technical leadership is directly relevant to
building and operating that foundation. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how I could
contribute to the fleet connectivity platform.
Best wishes,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
